commander: Major General Terry de la Mesa Allen
current_activity: first combat: moves into the line with the 1st British Corps on the south bank of the Maas
notes: Event date: 23 October 1944 (Siegfried p226: "only a day after the 104th Division first had moved into the line" on 24 October; the same page gives 1,400 casualties in its first action in the Netherlands). Event definition: the 104th Division, attached to the Canadian First Army, fights under Canadian First Army and British I Corps; the row dates its first entry into the line. Relationship: British I Corps operational_control and Canadian First Army operational_control from 15 October to 4 November (CMH table); Ninth Army administrative control. Location: Division command post at Westmalle on 22 October (atlas), the day before. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Westmalle. Event support: moderate (derived from a "day before 24 October" statement). Location support: moderate (command post listed one day earlier).

commander: Major General Terry de la Mesa Allen
current_activity: command post at Nordhausen; men of the division find the large underground V-2 factories outside the town
notes: Event date: 12 April 1945 (CMH ETO-OB command-post list of the 104th Infantry Division: Nordhausen on 12 Apr 45; Last Offensive ch. 17 p. 392: outside Nordhausen men of the 104th Division found large underground factories, one for manufacturing V-2 rockets, and the division began a march on Halle). Event definition: the division command post is at Nordhausen the day after the 3d Armored Division took the town; the row does not date the finding of the factories. Relationship: VII Corps unspecified_subordination (from 3 Feb 45, CMH table); First Army assigned (from 3 Feb 45, CMH table); 12th Army Group assigned (from 5 Nov 44, CMH table). The table entries start on the first row of the unbroken run (convention V-013). The CMH table has a single corps column and does not say assigned or attached for a corps. The earlier administrative_control relation to Ninth Army (CR0366) is closed at 2 February 1945 (inferred_from_next_claim); see the Review note on it. Location: Nordhausen (CMH ETO-OB command-post list, R339 p. 415: listed 12 April 1945); the town centre stands for the command post. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Nordhausen, Thuringia. Event support: moderate (one Green Book passage and the CMH table). Location support: moderate (command post listed on the date).

commander: Major General Terry de la Mesa Allen
current_activity: the 414th Infantry clears Halle after three days of house-to-house fighting; the other regiments turn east
notes: Event date: 19 April 1945 (Last Offensive ch. 17 p. 402: "For three more days, through the 19th, the 104th Division's 414th Infantry fought for Halle, killing or capturing unorganized three- to five-man groups in almost every building, while the division's other regiments turned east to conquer Bitterfeld and reach the Mulde River"). Event definition: the fight for the city ends on the 19th; the date is the last day of the three days the source gives. Relationship: VII Corps unspecified_subordination (from 3 Feb 45, CMH table); First Army assigned (from 3 Feb 45, CMH table); 12th Army Group assigned (from 5 Nov 44, CMH table). The table entries start on the first row of the unbroken run (convention V-013). The CMH table has a single corps column and does not say assigned or attached for a corps. Location: Halle (Saale), city centre standing for the objective. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Halle (Saale). Event support: moderate (one Green Book passage; the date is the last day of a stated range). Location support: moderate (named city).
